title: Typed-DSL Constrained Data Recipes for Higher Executability in DataChef

contributions.purpose: Identifies why DataChef's free-form Python data recipes so rarely execute successfully.
contributions.mechanism: Automated failure-mode audit on 50 independently-sampled recipes per task (Qwen3-32B generator), categorizing failures as DSL-addressable structural issues (syntax errors, format violations, invalid compositions, hallucinated datasets) versus non-DSL-addressable semantic ones.
contributions.evaluation: 45-61% of failures are structural and DSL-addressable (60.9% on ClimaQA, 44.2% on OpenFinData), with syntax errors alone accounting for 13-17%.
contributions.domain: automated data engineering / LLM data recipe generation
contributions.source_quote: A failure mode analysis validating that a majority of DataChef recipe failures are DSL-addressable structural issues.

contributions.purpose: Eliminates structural failure categories by constraining the recipe generation output space.
contributions.mechanism: A typed operator DSL where the model outputs JSON conforming to a JSON Schema of typed operators and dataset identifiers; a deterministic compiler converts validated DSL programs into executable Python, leveraging constrained decoding.
contributions.evaluation: Constrains generation to valid operator compositions while maintaining expressiveness; enables the executable-rate gains reported in C3.
contributions.source_quote: A typed operator DSL with JSON Schema validation that constrains recipe generation to valid operator compositions while maintaining expressiveness.

contributions.purpose: Quantifies the executability and reward gains from typed-DSL constrained generation.
contributions.mechanism: End-to-end comparison of typed-DSL constrained generation against free-form Python generation in the DataChef RL framework, plus ablations separating typed operator constraints from structured JSON output format.
contributions.evaluation: 5.8-29x improvement in executable rate (from 3-16% to 90.6%), 8.4-34.1x improvement in DVS_avg@32, 84.5% reduction in total failures; ablations confirm typed operator constraints, not JSON format, are the key mechanism.
contributions.domain: automated data engineering / LLM data recipe generation
contributions.source_quote: Experimental results demonstrating 5.8-29x improvement in executable rate and 8.4-34.1x improvement in DVS_avg@32, with ablations confirming that typed operators (not JSON format) are the key mechanism.

self_declared_provenance.quote: These systems focus on operator abstractions but do not constrain an RL-trained code generator's action space. Our work applies typed-DSL constraints specifically to improve the executability of LLM-generated data recipes.
Our work applies these structured generation principles to data recipe generation, demonstrating that typed operator constraints can dramatically improve executability in this domain.
This approach leverages recent advances in constrained decoding (Willard & Louf, 2023; Dong et al., 2024) to efficiently enforce schema validity during generation.

notes: Positive-result paper. Builds directly on DataChef (Chen et al., 2026); the contribution is applying existing constrained-decoding/DSL principles to that framework. Improvement baselines start from very low executability (3-16%).
